summary: Atezolizumab (Tecentriq) is an anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibody that releases PD-L1/PD-1 and PD-L1/B7.1 mediated inhibition of the antitumor immune response. It is given by IV infusion as 840 mg every 2 weeks, 1200 mg every 3 weeks, or 1680 mg every 4 weeks, alone or with other agents, for several cancers including non-small cell and small cell lung cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, melanoma, and alveolar soft part sarcoma. The defining safety concern is severe and fatal IMMUNE-MEDIATED ADVERSE REACTIONS that can affect ANY organ system - including pneumonitis, colitis, hepatitis, endocrinopathies (thyroid disorders, adrenal insufficiency, hypophysitis, type 1 diabetes), nephritis, dermatologic reactions (including SJS/TEN), myocarditis and neurologic reactions - which require prompt evaluation, withholding or permanent discontinuation, and corticosteroids. Infusion-related reactions and embryo-fetal toxicity are additional risks.
indications: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) - first-line, maintenance, and adjuvant settings per current labeling, alone or in combination
Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) - first-line with carboplatin and etoposide
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) - in patients not previously treated with systemic therapy, in combination with bevacizumab
Unresectable or metastatic melanoma with BRAF V600 mutation - in combination with cobimetinib and vemurafenib
Unresectable or metastatic alveolar soft part sarcoma (ASPS) in adults and pediatric patients 2 years and older

dosage.d: 840 mg IV every 2 weeks, OR 1200 mg IV every 3 weeks, OR 1680 mg IV every 4 weeks
dosage.n: Select one schedule; first infusion over 60 min, then over 30 min if tolerated

dosage.d: Per the specific regimen (e.g., with carboplatin/etoposide, bevacizumab, or cobimetinib/vemurafenib); give atezolizumab first when combined on the same day
dosage.n: Follow the combination-agent prescribing information for the partner drugs

dosage.c: Pediatric - alveolar soft part sarcoma (2 yrs and older)
dosage.d: Under 18 yrs: 15 mg/kg (max 1200 mg) IV every 3 weeks
dosage.n: Adults with ASPS: 1200 mg IV every 3 weeks

dosage.d: Withhold or permanently discontinue based on severity; administer corticosteroids (e.g., 1-2 mg/kg/day prednisone or equivalent) and taper
dosage.n: No dose reduction; manage by withholding or stopping per severity grade

admin: Administer only by intravenous infusion through a sterile, non-pyrogenic, low-protein-binding in-line filter (0.2 to 0.22 micron)
Do NOT administer as an IV push or bolus
Infuse the first dose over 60 minutes; if the first infusion is tolerated, subsequent infusions may be given over 30 minutes
Do not co-administer other drugs through the same infusion line
When given with other antineoplastic agents on the same day, administer atezolizumab first per the regimen
Dilute in 0.9% sodium chloride per the prescribing information; inspect for particulates
moa: Atezolizumab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) and blocks its interactions with the PD-1 and B7.1 (CD80) receptors. PD-L1 expressed on tumor cells and tumor-infiltrating immune cells normally suppresses cytotoxic T-cell activity. By releasing PD-L1/PD-1 and PD-L1/B7.1-mediated inhibition of the immune response, atezolizumab reactivates antitumor T-cell immunity, reducing tumor growth.

absolute: None listed in labeling (no absolute contraindications)
relative: History of severe hypersensitivity or infusion reaction to atezolizumab
Prior allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant or solid organ transplant (risk of rejection/GVHD)
monitor: Signs/symptoms of immune-mediated reactions in any organ system
Infusion-related reactions during and after administration
Liver enzymes, thyroid function, blood glucose and adrenal/pituitary function

preg: Based on its mechanism and animal data, atezolizumab can cause fetal harm and is associated with increased abortion and stillbirth in animal studies (PD-L1/PD-1 pathway is important for maintaining pregnancy). Advise patients of the risk and verify pregnancy status before starting; females of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for 5 months after the last dose.
lact: There are no data on the presence of atezolizumab in human milk or its effects on the breastfed infant. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 5 months after the last dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is recommended for patients with renal impairment. Population analyses found mild to moderate renal impairment had no clinically meaningful effect on exposure; severe impairment data are limited.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is recommended for mild hepatic impairment; data in moderate to severe impairment are limited. Because immune-mediated hepatitis can occur, monitor liver enzymes and bilirubin regularly and manage hepatic immune-mediated reactions by withholding or discontinuing and giving corticosteroids.

major: No formal pharmacokinetic drug-drug interaction studies; as a monoclonal antibody it is not metabolized by CYP enzymes
moderate: Systemic corticosteroids or immunosuppressants before starting - may blunt efficacy; use for replacement (e.g., adrenal) or to treat immune-mediated reactions is appropriate
Live vaccines - avoid during checkpoint inhibitor therapy due to immune activation
minor: Combination antineoplastic partners (carboplatin/etoposide, bevacizumab, cobimetinib/vemurafenib) - additive toxicities per their labels
interactions.food: Not applicable - intravenous infusion, not affected by food.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction with atezolizumab; advise limiting alcohol if there are hepatic concerns or immune-mediated hepatitis.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause immune-mediated elevations in liver enzymes, abnormal thyroid function tests, hyperglycemia, and abnormal cortisol/ACTH; tumor PD-L1 expression testing guides certain indications.

serious: Immune-mediated endocrinopathies (thyroid disorders, adrenal insufficiency, hypophysitis, type 1 diabetes mellitus)
Immune-mediated neurologic reactions (myasthenic syndrome, Guillain-Barre, meningoencephalitis)
Complications of allogeneic HSCT (GVHD, hepatic veno-occlusive disease)
emergency: Severe or life-threatening pneumonitis (new/worsening dyspnea, hypoxia)
Diabetic ketoacidosis from new type 1 diabetes

monitoring: Assess for signs and symptoms of immune-mediated reactions in ANY organ system at each visit (any new symptom may be immune-mediated)
Monitor for pneumonitis (chest imaging as indicated), colitis, and hepatitis (liver enzymes and bilirubin)
Thyroid function, blood glucose, and adrenal/pituitary function (cortisol, ACTH) at baseline and periodically
Observe for infusion-related reactions during and after each infusion
Verify pregnancy status in females of reproductive potential before initiation
counsel: This is an immunotherapy that can cause your immune system to attack normal organs - report ANY new or worsening symptom promptly
Seek urgent care for new cough or trouble breathing, chest pain, severe diarrhea or abdominal pain, yellowing of skin/eyes, severe rash or blisters, excessive thirst/urination, or confusion
Tell your team about prior organ or stem cell transplant and any autoimmune disease
Do not become pregnant; use effective contraception during and for 5 months after the last dose
Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 5 months after the last dose
Keep all scheduled infusion appointments; report symptoms even between visits
pk: Immediate immune effect; antitumor response over weeks to months
Steady state by ~6-9 weeks; dosing q2w, q3w, or q4w
Refrigerate vials at 2-8 C (36-46 F); do not freeze or shake; protect from light
pearls: Immune-mediated adverse reactions can occur in ANY organ system, at any time during or even after stopping therapy - maintain a high index of suspicion for any new symptom
Management of immune-mediated reactions: withhold or permanently discontinue based on severity and give systemic corticosteroids with a taper
Endocrinopathies (thyroid, adrenal insufficiency, hypophysitis, type 1 diabetes) may present subtly - check thyroid, glucose, and adrenal/pituitary function periodically
Three interchangeable schedules (840 mg q2w, 1200 mg q3w, 1680 mg q4w) give flexibility; first infusion 60 min then 30 min if tolerated
Embryo-fetal toxicity - the PD-L1/PD-1 pathway maintains pregnancy; ensure effective contraception
missed: Atezolizumab infusions are scheduled and administered by the oncology team. There is no patient self-dosing; if a dose is missed or delayed, it should be given as soon as possible and the subsequent dosing schedule adjusted by the treating clinician to maintain the appropriate interval between doses.
overdose: There is no information on overdose with atezolizumab and no specific antidote. In the event of overdose, monitor closely for signs or symptoms of adverse reactions - particularly immune-mediated and infusion-related reactions - and institute appropriate supportive treatment.
